title: Traffic Morphing Fabricator and Shadow Triage Playbook
author: Avery Chen
summary: Operational playbook for creating, injecting, and triaging synthetic traffic ("morphs") used to validate model-onboardings, quantized rollouts, and regression hunting across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the Traffic Morphing Fabricator (TMF) — a lightweight service and set of procedures used by Applied ML and SRE teams to generate realistic, controllable shadow traffic for: model onboarding, quantization safety checks, eval harness stress testing, and regression triage. TMF focuses on morphing live telemetry into targeted probe cohorts while preserving privacy and controlling cost.

Goals
- Produce shadow traffic that closely matches production distribution slices relevant to a deployment (latency-sensitive, KV-cache-heavy, functioncall-heavy, rare-edge intents).
- Allow deterministic amplification, attenuation, and priming of traffic for safety-oriented rollouts (quantized artifacts, prompt-sensitive regressions).
- Provide clear triage signals and guardrails for automatic escalation and rollback.

When to use TMF
- Before a canary or full rollout of a new model variant (quantized or architecture change).
- To reproduce a regression that only appears under particular prompt-distribution skews.
- Running preflight on Dedicated/Private deployments where customer traffic is ephemeral or unavailable.

Key concepts and definitions
- Morph: a single generated request derived from production telemetry (may be sampled, condensed, or augmented).
- Cohort: a named group of morphs that represent a behavioral slice (e.g., "kv-cache-hot", "functioncall-heavy", "longcontext-legal" ).
- Priming: deterministic prefixing of prompts to exercise model behaviors (used for functioncall stability tests).
- Amplification factor: integer multiplier that increases sample frequency for a cohort.
- Quiet window: a deployment period where amplified shadowing is restricted to avoid billing surprises.

Ownership and roles
- TMF Service Owner: Applied ML Platform (primary contact: @applied-ml-platform).
- Experiment Lead: ML engineer proposing the morph cohort and acceptance criteria.
- Oncall SRE: monitors infrastructure and enforces rate limits/cost policies during tests.
- Security Reviewer: approves cohort composition if it includes PII-sensitive tokens.

Service-level inputs (minimum required before a run)
1) Cohort manifest (YAML): name, seed-query-set-id, amplification, injection-mode (shadow|fork), preservation-level (hashed|redacted).
2) Acceptance criteria: latency SLO delta, quality threshold (response-stability-index), embedding-similarity floor for semantic equivalence.
3) Cost cap: maximum simulated tokens / wall-time budget.

Example cohort manifest (YAML)
---
cohort_name: kv-cache-hot-morphs
seed_source: telemetry-seedset-2027-02
amplification: 8
injection_mode: shadow
preservation: hashed
priming_template: |
  System: "You are a Redwood inference test harness. Answer concisely."
  User: "{seed_prompt}"
acceptance: |
  - rsi_min: 0.92
  - latency_p99_delta_ms: 30
  - token_cost_limit: 500000
---

CLI quickstart (tmfctl)
1) Create manifest file: tmfctl manifest create --file kv-cache-hot.yml
2) Dry-run (no downstream injection): tmfctl run --manifest kv-cache-hot.yml --mode dry-run
3) Start shadow injection (observability enabled): tmfctl run --manifest kv-cache-hot.yml --mode inject --notify on-start

Observability and telemetry (minimum dashboards)
- TMF /run/{cohort}/throughput: morphs/sec, amplification factor applied.
- model/response_stability_index: cohort-tagged RSI per model-variant.
- model/latency_p{50,95,99}_delta_ms: delta vs baseline variant.
- cost/accounted_tokens: token spend attributed to TMF-run (broken down by cohort).

Prometheus example alerts (text)
- ALERT: TMF_RSI_DROP
  WHEN: model_response_stability_index{cohort="kv-cache-hot"} < 0.9 for 5m
  ACTION: auto-stop cohort injection + notify regression-oncall + create incident ticket

Quality guardrails (hard gates)
- If RSI < 0.9 or embedding-similarity < 0.88 on any cohort, TMF must auto-pause and trigger the regression triage workflow.
- Latency p99 delta > configured SLO gap (default 40ms) triggers pause for Dedicated/private runs.
- Token-cost consumption exceeding the cohort token limit (manifest) triggers soft-throttle (reduce amplification) and notify finance.

Quantization-aware considerations
- When morphing for quantized rollouts: include quant-specific stress probes (noise-perturbation prompts, numeric precision checks, few-shot coherence anchors).
- Add a quant-fingerprint tag to morphs to collect per-token internal flops per model.
- Recommended quant baseline test: run amplification=4 with priming templates and verify coherence-first metric (CohFirst >= 0.93) before canary.

Integration with eval harness and prompt catalogs
- Seed sets should be produced by the Eval Harness sample registry and annotated with probe slice metadata. Use the prompt-catalog id in the manifest.
- For functioncall-heavy cohorts, attach a small function definition bundle to the manifest to validate functioncall stability end-to-end.

Regression triage workflow (numbered quick-run)
1) Detection: Alerting triggers when RSI or latency gates are violated. An incident is opened with the cohort id and the TMF-run id.
2) Auto-pause: TMF pauses injection and snapshots last 500 morphs to artifact storage (redacted as required).
3) Initial hypothesis: Operator runs the TMF triage helper to compute quick diffs (token-level divergence, functioncall-failure-rate, embedding-shift histogram).
   tmfctl triage quick-diff --run {run_id} --out /tmp/triage.json
4) Blame routing: If diffs point to quant-fingerprint variance, route to the Quant Triage team; if prompt-anchored drift, route to Prompt Steward; else open SRE investigation.
5) Rollback or mitigation: Depending on the severity, either rollback the canary route or apply an automatic prompt rewrite guard and resume with amplification=1 for 30 minutes.
6) Postmortem: Owner creates a regression postmortem drafting the root cause, corrective actions, and probe updates. Attach TMF artifacts and eval-harness replays.

Investigation helpers and tooling outputs
- tmfctl extract --run {run_id} --slice kv-cache-hot --format ndjson -> produces per-morph trace including: seed_hash, primed_prompt, response_tokens, model_variant, quant_fingerprint
- quick-diff output fields (CSV): seed_hash, baseline_similarity, candidate_similarity, latency_delta_ms, functioncall_drop

Cost controls and billing policy
- All TMF runs must include a cost cap in manifest. Any run exceeding 80% cap emits a billing-warning to finance and leads.
- Dedicated/private runs have stricter multipliers (max amplification 4) unless approved by SRE + finance.

Privacy and PII handling
- TMF must never inject raw PII. Seed sets must run through the PII-scrubber step (PII redaction hash). Manifests must declare preservation: hashed|redacted.
- Security review required for any cohort that uses customer-supplied seeds.

Acceptance checklist before promoting a model that passed TMF runs
- All cohort acceptance criteria green for 72 hours at amplification >= 2.
- No alerts triggered for RSI, embedding-similarity, or latency.
- Quant-fingerprint drift within allowed window (<0.03 normalised variance).
- Annotation spot-check: at least 50 sampled morph responses have human QA confirm semantic parity.

Runbook: emergency rollback (quick)
1) tmfctl run pause --id {run_id}
2) Model routing: set traffic back to last-known-good variant (api call or console route).
3) Notify customers if private/dedicated customers affected (use escalation playbook).
4) Start post-incident shadow with amplification=1 to validate rollback sufficiency.

Appendix A — Sample JSON payload (morph)
{
  "seed_hash": "sha256:abc123...",
  "primed_prompt": "System: ... User: ...",
  "cohort": "kv-cache-hot",
  "metadata": "redacted",
  "injected_at": "2027-02-14T18:22:00Z"
}

Appendix B — Common failure modes & mitigations
- Mode: Functioncall parser mismatch under quantized weights. Mitigation: run functioncall-priming probe set and increase float-stability threshold or revert quant profile.
- Mode: KV-cache behavioral divergence. Mitigation: regenerate morphs with longer context priming and reduce amplification.
- Mode: Cost runaway due to amplification misconfiguration. Mitigation: enforce hard tokens cap and auto-terminate when exceeded.
